subject: Re: Dedicated GPU queueing / throughput SLO carveout - CloudMason
content:
--- Message 1/6 ---
From: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@cloudmason.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU queueing / throughput SLO carveout

Hi Priya,

Following up from our QBR: CloudMason is targeting a heavy seasonal ramp across our inference pipeline (fraud detection) starting March 1. Our current dedicated pool (48 reserved GPUs) is hitting sustained tail queueing at peak hours and we're seeing 20–30% request spillover to lower tiers which is causing unacceptable tail latency for critical flows.

We'd like to request a temporary carveout to the Dedicated SLA that ensures:
- minimum effective throughput at peak (per-minute token throughput guarantee)
- queueing priority for two production queues (fraud-realtime, fraud-batch) with preemption protection for X% of the pool
- a defined incident credit/recourse if sustained queueing above threshold (>= 5% of minutes in peak hour) persists for more than one week

Can Redwood propose an operational playbook and SLO addendum for a 3-month pilot (Mar–May) so we can validate behavior pre-commitment? Contracts team copied.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Malik
Head of Infrastructure, CloudMason
--- Message 2/6 ---
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated GPU queueing / throughput SLO carveout

Karthik / Marcus — forwarding CloudMason's ask. They need a short-term carveout to avoid spillover to non-dedicated capacity during a heavy ramp. Key asks above.

Can we:
1) confirm feasibility to reserve X% (they called out preemption protection for two queues) — how would this map to our pool scheduling?
2) propose a pilot SLO and credit structure (they want incident credit if queueing persists)
3) provide any required telemetry/feed we need from them (metrics, token profiles) — they offered queueing-metrics.csv in their email thread (cc'd contracts).

I'll own the external comms if you draft the addendum.

-Priya
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
--- Message 3/6 ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated GPU queueing / throughput SLO carveout

Priya — quick read: technically doable but needs a narrowly scoped approach to avoid destabilizing the pool. Proposed items from infra: 

- Carveout model: reserve a hard slice of capacity (e.g., 10 GPUs) pinned for preempt-protected queues, plus a soft headroom buffer (approx 15% of pool) that can be borrowed with >30s warmup.
- Queueing semantics: implement weighted fair queuing with queue weights pinned to the two production queues and a tail-latency monitor that triggers automatic request shedding to lower-priority routes once sustained queueing exceed threshold.
- Measurement: minutes-over-threshold (MOT) metric aggregated per peak hour.

Constraints: if we hard-pin GPUs we may impact other customers' burst capacity; we should limit pilot to 3 months and tie to usage band (48 GPUs qualifies). Also need their token-length distribution (they said they'd attach metrics).

If you want, I can produce a short SLO blurb and runbook.

-Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime
--- Message 4/6 ---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 11:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated GPU queueing / throughput SLO carveout

On the commercial side: recommend a pilot addendum that includes:
- 3-month pilot (no change to base commitment), with explicit exit criteria.
- SLA credit formula: fixed credit equal to 10% of the monthly Dedicated commitment per week where MOT > 5% in peak hours, capped at one full monthly credit for the pilot period.
- Option to convert pilot behaviors into a permanent addendum with negotiated price uplift if CloudMason wants hard capacity reservation after pilot.

Also suggest we require CloudMason to supply the minute-level telemetry (queueing-metrics.csv) and a contact for acceleration windows. We'll attach a proposed-slo-addendum.pdf I drafted for similar pilots and tweak per Karthik's runbook.

-Marcus
Head of Revenue Operations
--- Message 5/6 ---
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@cloudmason.com>
Cc: contracts@cloudmason.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU queueing / throughput SLO carveout

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the metrics. Attached is a proposed SLO addendum and a short runbook (proposed-slo-addendum.pdf). Summary of what Redwood proposes for the 3-month pilot (Mar 1–May 31):

1) Capacity carveout: 10 GPUs hard-reserved for preempt-protected queues (fraud-realtime, fraud-batch) + 15% soft headroom across the 48-GPU pool.
2) Queueing behavior: weighted fair queueing with a tail-latency monitor. If minutes-over-threshold (MOT) >= 5% in any peak hour for two consecutive days, Redwood will trigger mitigation actions (auto-burst to standby capacity, prioritize preempt-protected queues).
3) Credits: for any week where MOT > 5% for more than 60 mins total during defined peak windows, CloudMason receives a credit equal to 10% of their monthly Dedicated invoice, up to a single full monthly credit for the pilot.
4) Telemetry: CloudMason to provide minute-level queueing-metrics.csv and token distribution by Feb 26 so we can calibrate burst targets.

Attachments: proposed-slo-addendum.pdf (legal + runbook), queueing-metrics.csv (their telemetry). Please confirm you can provide the telemetry by the 26th and whether the pilot window is acceptable. If so, we'll route the addendum to our contracts team for signature.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
--- Message 6/6 ---
From: Aisha Malik <aisha.malik@cloudmason.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@cloudmason.com
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU queueing / throughput SLO carveout

Thanks Priya — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. We can provide the minute-level telemetry and token distribution by Feb 26. Pilot window (Mar 1–May 31) is fine. Our contracts team is standing by to review the proposed-slo-addendum.pdf; please route.

One operational ask: can we get a pre-launch validation window (Mar 1–Mar 3) where Redwood runs headroom tuning against our replay traffic before we flip the production routing? That will help reduce surprise shedding.

If you can add that 72-hour validation step to the runbook and flag any config items we need to change, we can sign quickly.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Aisha Malik
Head of Infrastructure, CloudMason
